rationale: The compiled seed edits, bindings, selector, and cards faithfully instantiate the design. The three new message_reactions rows (raised_hands on the core-infra OOM alert by U_LUKAS, thumbsup on the login-failure message by U03ROBERT23, raised_hands on the context-growth message by U_PRIYA) match exactly what the design specified, and the pre-existing eyes reaction is unchanged. The selector's filters (messages.message_text contains 'OOM', users.real_name contains 'Robert', joined via message_reactions→messages→channels→channel_members→users) correctly separate the two genuine matches from the two negatives: verified against the actual message texts, only 1706110000.000100 ('...hitting OOM errors...') and 1706000208.000000 ('...OOM kills detected.') contain the substring 'OOM', while the login-failure message and the context-growth message do not, so the negatives are excluded by the filter itself rather than by a hidden hand-picked exclusion — a clean, non-hint-leaking construction. Both qualifying channels (engineering C03IJKL9012, core-infra C_INFRA) have a real 'Robert' member confirmed in channel_members (U03ROBERT23, U_ROBERT), and a scan of all messages in both channels (and Robert Chen's other channels) confirms no third OOM-report candidate exists, so the two-way ambiguity is exact and matches the target_roles/candidate_role_sets. The acting user (U01AGENBOT9) is already a member of both relevant channels, giving realistic, non-hidden-ID access via conversations.history/reactions.get consistent with the documented API. Mechanical checks report no errors, and computed_matches/negatives/candidate_population align exactly with the private expected_matches and near_misses. This is a well-formed underspecified case: a singular prompt phrase legitimately maps to two structurally symmetric, equally valid answers with meaningful topic-based negatives, and the compiler introduced only the necessary new reaction rows as anticipated by the design review.
